chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Abdullah ibn Ahmad al-Nahiki, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Bishr ibn Maslama, from Abu al-Hasan al-Reza (peace be upon him), regarding

a kid (baby goat) that had been breast-fed from a female pig (sow) and was then let loose among the flock. He said: 'It is at the status of cheese. So whatever you recognize as having been mated by it, do not eat it; and whatever you do not recognize, eat it.'

key_terms.جَدْي: Kid/baby goat — the subject animal whose status is being determined
key_terms.خِنْزِيرَة: Female pig/sow — a ritually impure (najis) animal whose milk renders what feeds from it doubtful
key_terms.ضَرَبَ فِي الغَنَم: Was put among the flock — the goat was released into the herd making identification of its offspring uncertain
key_terms.مَنْزِلَة الجُبُنّ: Status of cheese — cheese analogy refers to the legal principle that products of unclear origin default to permissibility unless contamination is known

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating a goat that was nursed by a pig according to Imam al-Reza?
ai.summary: Imam al-Reza (AS) addressed a jurisprudential question about the ritual purity status of a baby goat that nursed from a pig. He ruled that such an animal is analogous to cheese made with rennet of uncertain origin: the default state is permissible to eat unless one specifically knows it has been mixed (mated with other animals). This ruling reflects the Shia legal principle of defaulting to permissibility when specific contamination cannot be confirmed.
word_analysis: mated with it/was mixed with it

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Abdullah Bin Ahmad Al Naheyki, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Bishr Bin Maslama, (It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> regarding

a baby goat who was breast-fed from a female pig, then it was connected among the flock. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is at the status of the cheese. So whatever is recognised as being connected with it, so do not eat it, and whatever is not recognised, so eat it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ahmad al-Nuhaykiy from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Bishr ibn Muslimah who has said the following: “About the case of a young goat that is fed with the milk of a pig and it is used to impregnate the flock of sheep, abu al-Hassan, al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘It is like cheese. If you recognize its offspring exactly, then do not eat; but you can eat if you cannot recognize it.’”
